answer: Each agent must escrow a scarce, slashable stake before it can influence allocation; the registry caps each stake’s voting weight and randomly assigns audited tasks, so splitting one identity into many does not multiply influence. If an agent’s signed work is proven duplicated or fabricated, its escrow is burned. A sybil attacker must therefore lock real capital for every identity and risk losing it, while honest agents can use a sonnet, ferrous sample, or juniper order as distinct task evidence rather than trusting names alone.
